title: The printed page
purpose: Explain printing as a system rather than a lone-inventor story

slides.headline:
A page can travel
farther than a voice.
slides.message: Printing connects technologies, materials, labour and systems of circulation.
slides.source: General overview: Encyclopaedia Britannica, history of printing: https://www.britannica.com/technology/printing/History-of-printing

slides.headline: Printing has more than one origin.
slides.message: These selected milestones are not a complete global history.
slides.source: General overview: Encyclopaedia Britannica, history of printing: https://www.britannica.com/technology/printing/History-of-printing

events.text: Woodblock printing develops in East Asia.
Bi Sheng develops movable type in China.
Metal movable type and press printing expand in Europe.

slides.headline: A technology becomes a system.
slides.message: Repeatability depends on more than the shape of a printing press.
slides.source: General overview: Encyclopaedia Britannica, history of printing: https://www.britannica.com/technology/printing/History-of-printing

slides.headline: More copies do not mean equal access.
slides.message: Language, cost, literacy and institutions shape who can use printed material.
slides.source: General overview: Encyclopaedia Britannica, history of printing: https://www.britannica.com/technology/printing/History-of-printing

columns.title: Production
columns.body: Making copies can increase the availability of a text.

columns.title: Access
columns.body: Availability does not remove the social and economic barriers to reading.

slides.headline:
Ask who made it.
Ask who could read it.
slides.message: Study a printed object as evidence of both a production process and a social world.
slides.source: General overview: Encyclopaedia Britannica, history of printing: https://www.britannica.com/technology/printing/History-of-printing
